text:
mina: seeing a surprising uptick in fncall validation.rejections for tool-bridge.v2 in us-central after the strict-schema rollout. looks like some adapters are dropping optional objects entirely -> validator rejects. anyone have context?

dan: that's the new strict shape enforcement. adapters that used to return `null` or omit fields are now getting hard rejects.

lee: sample log: {error:EVAL_FN_09, path:response.metadata, expected:object, got:null} - adapter `bridge-legacy` omitted metadata when cache empty.

mina: quick options: 1) rollback strict enforcement 2) enable per-route `soft-coerce` to synthesize minimal objects + emit warnings 3) route traffic to permissive variant.

dan: prefer #2. we can surface provenance (`validation.provenance`) and diff in console so owners see exactly what was coerced.

console-team: UX: add a small "coercions" column in the route table, and in the request inspector show an inline before/after diff. also show a badge when coercions > 0.5% for 15m.

ops-bot: Alert: validation.reject rate > 0.6% on route fncall.tool-bridge.v2 (us-central)  incident #INC-7944 created.

billing-bot: note: if we perform coercion server-side, we need a billing policy. by default flagged responses will be `billing_review`. finance prefers CSV export of affected request_ids.

lee: roll plan: enable `soft-coerce` on fncall.tool-bridge.v2 canary slice=10% with tags ["validation_softcoerce","canary:10pct"], sample 200 payloads/hr, retention 48h. responses include `validation.warnings` and `validation.provenance` array.

mina: agreed. also add `validation.mode` metric and `coercion_count` counter to telemetry so console can chart it. make coerced responses annotated `billing_review=true`.

dan: impl note: validator will synthesize minimal object using schema defaults where available; for unknown optional fields we synthesize `{}` and log path. not doing heavy merging.

console-team: will add a temporary banner: "Soft-coerce active on fncall.tool-bridge.v2 (canary) - affected requests marked billing_review" and a link to the incident.

ops-bot: Update: soft-coerce toggled on canary at 04:12 UTC. reject rate dropped ~75% in 10m.

mina: leaving open until adapter owners patch. next steps: retro to add adapter shape tests in CI, decide final billing treatment (auto-adjust vs manual review), and consider adding a `coercion_provenance` header for end-to-end tracing.

dan: adding CI testcases: omit field / null field / empty object / empty array permutations. will open PR.

lee: will coordinate with adapter team to patch bridge-legacy. ETA 2h.

mina: thanks all. I'll update incident when adapters patched or if rates spike. :thumbsup:
